newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasoline gets boost from heating oil.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasoline gets boost from heating oil.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot unleaded gasoline got a boost from soaring heating oil futures early Monday, as forecasts of an extended cold snap in several U.S. regions raised concerns about supply tightness.
AT 1110 PST, heating oil traded about 75.15 cents a gallon, up 3.44 cents from Friday's market.
Heating oil propelled NYMEX January gasoline up 2.66 cents a gallon to 69.70 cents and lifted front-month crude up $1.36 a barrel to $25.80.
West Coast spot trade followed NYMEX, brokers said, with a cargo of January gasoline selling in Los Angeles for 71 cents.
Barrels of December conventional regular unleaded gasoline rose 1.75 cents a gallon in Los Angeles to 69.75/70.75 cents a gallon, brokers said.
Bids for low sulphur diesel fuel rose 2.50 cents a gallon to 69 cents, while offers jumped 2.25 cents to 69.75 cents. January barrels ranged 0.75 cents a gallon higher, traders said.
Bay-area gasolines stood about 1.75 cents a gallon lower than L.A. material, traders said.
